Gal*Gun: Double Peace was a surprisingly enjoyable experience from beginning to end. What initially looks like a simple anime rail shooter quickly reveals a game with a surprising amount of content, replay value, and charm. The gameplay is easy to learn but remains fun throughout multiple playthroughs, especially when aiming for higher ranks, Perfect boss battles, and achievement completion. The cast is one of the game's strongest points, with characters like Shinobu, Maya, Kurona, and Patako each having their own unique personalities and memorable story routes. The humor is over-the-top and self-aware, which fits the game's style perfectly and keeps the experience entertaining.

What impressed me the most was how much there is to do beyond a single playthrough. Unlocking different endings, collecting character data, finding hidden content, and completing achievements gave me many reasons to keep playing. The boss fights can be surprisingly challenging, especially when going for Perfect scores, and achievements like Gal*God provide a satisfying challenge for completionists. The voice acting and soundtrack also do a great job of bringing the characters and scenes to life, making the overall presentation much stronger than I expected.

While the game is definitely aimed at fans of anime and lighthearted comedy, it offers far more depth and replayability than it may appear to have at first glance. If you enjoy character-driven stories, arcade-style gameplay, and hunting for 100% completion, Gal*Gun: Double Peace is a very fun and rewarding experience that is worth your time. I had a great time with it and would happily recommend it to anyone interested in the series. 9/10.

I'm a little conflicted about this game. I wish Steam had a "Mixed" option for cases like this, but I'll try my best.

For full price, I'm going to say No. With a discount, I'd say Yes depending on the percentage.

One look at my library would tell any casual observer that I enjoy the... raunchier side of Steam's store. In spite of that, I'm not really sure how much I can say I like this game. This is my first Gal Gun experience and the only thing I can seriously say I enjoy about it is the perverted nature of the content, whether that be looking up the various students' skirts or using the zoom feature that conveniently comes with X-Ray vision... believe me, this type of game is built for people like me, which is also what makes this review slightly difficult to write.

I do actually appreciate that the characters have personalities beyond just giving the player something to look at. Every girl has a particular weakspot for both general gameplay and Doki Doki Mode, meaning there's an incentive to learn and adapt to each girl on the fly.

The graphics are... well, apparently this game is a port from the Xbox 360. It certainly looks like it, at least. The models of the various characters do look decent, especially when you buy the Angel Eye Drops... however, the game often moves and shifts perspective too quickly for you to be able to really enjoy what's on display. That makes it feel like wasted potential, at least to me.

The music is pretty much what you'd expect from any other anime game. Nothing special.

Mechanics are simple but I can tell there's a high level of skill expression that can be shown if you're into that sort of thing.

The main thing that kind of puts me off are the dialogue choices and endings. The game tasks you with keeping track of your character's stats, which seems to determine the choices that are available to you. The problem here is that the game in no way explains or even really hints at how this works. The most you get is some kind of sound effect when you choose something. Sometimes you don't get a sound effect at all, which I can only assume means "neutral". Without a guide, you'll just be guessing most of the time. Grinding your stats is also a chore. I'm not even really sure how you're meant to do it besides buying the relevant items in the shop. As far as I can tell, using Doki Doki mode on certain girls will boost some stats and lower others, but I can't tell if it's based on how you touch them or what type of girl(s) you end up using the mode on... I have no clue. For all I know, it's entirely random.

The actual endings themselves range from okay to mediocre, and since you can't really tell what's a good choice or not (you have up to 5 at any given interaction), this resulted in me getting crappy endings more often than not. If I want an actually satisfying ending, I'd have to read a guide for it because otherwise there's just such a lack of feedback on what's a good choice or not. And if you screw up a route, chances are you'll have to play the entire route from scratch. Not really a fan of that. For reference, I currently have 3 endings unlocked (Maya, Aoi, and what I assume was the bad ending for the demon girl, but to be fair, I deliberately chose perverted dialogues with her just for comedic value).

I don't want this review to come off too negative, but honestly, there isn't a whole lot I can say is positive here. I mean, it's entertaining for a short while, and the characters have some charm to them, but at the end of the day, it's an overpriced game from a bygone era even when it came out on the 360, so... I'd give it a pass unless it's heavily discounted.

I don't believe the game is particularly bad per say, just... eh? I'll chip away at the endings as, if nothing else, the game makes for a decent break from my long sessions on American Truck Simulator. Outside of that though, I don't see myself sticking with this title for very long.

GalGun: Double Peace* is an on-rails shooter developed by Inti Creates, continuing the arcade-style structure of its predecessor. The game adapts traditional shooting mechanics to a linear, stage-based progression system, focusing on fast reactions, target prioritization, and scoring accuracy. It functions as a compact, timing-based action title rather than a full exploration game.

Gameplay follows a predictable rail-shooter formula: the player’s movement is automated while aiming and shooting manually. Each level presents waves of incoming targets and occasional mini-boss encounters. Scoring depends on accuracy, hit timing, and identifying weak points. The design rewards memorization and consistent precision.

The control system is responsive across both controller and mouse inputs. Calibration options allow fine-tuning of aiming sensitivity, improving consistency compared to earlier entries. The difficulty curve is gentle, making it accessible to casual players while still providing challenge in higher modes.

Visually, GalGun: Double Peace* uses a bright, stylized 3D anime aesthetic. Environments are colorful, simple, and designed for quick readability during fast-paced sequences. The framerate is stable, and load times are short. Performance across platforms remains smooth even during dense action.

Audio complements the visual tone with light, upbeat music and short sound cues. The mix emphasizes clarity over realism, and the sound design serves a primarily functional purpose—tracking hits and giving quick feedback to the player.

The structure includes multiple routes and endings, giving moderate replay value. While narrative depth is minimal, route selection and performance rankings add incentive for repeated runs. Between missions, brief dialogue scenes provide context and pacing without extending playtime unnecessarily.

Overall, GalGun: Double Peace* is a competent and polished rail shooter. It offers fast reaction-based gameplay, accessible controls, and smooth technical execution. For players who enjoy short, arcade-style shooters with branching routes and light narrative framing, it performs its function effectively within its limited scope.

Gal*Gun: Double Peace is a unique blend of on-rails shooting gameplay and anime-style visual novel storytelling that embraces its eccentric premise with unapologetic enthusiasm. Developed by Inti Creates and published by PQube, the game centers around Houdai Kudoki, a high school student who becomes the accidental target of a love arrow gone haywire, causing every girl at his school to fall madly in love with him. This absurd setup creates a chaotic but humorous atmosphere where the player must fend off a barrage of overly affectionate classmates using a pheromone gun, all while trying to find their true love before the day ends. The premise is certainly unconventional, mixing romance, comedy, and action in a way that few games dare to attempt.

Gameplay in Gal*Gun: Double Peace is straightforward yet surprisingly engaging. The player navigates through various school-themed levels on rails, aiming and shooting at heart-shaped weak points on characters to calm their advances. Each successful shot fills a meter that, when maxed out, triggers a special “Doki-Doki Mode,” featuring a flashy and somewhat risqué sequence unique to each character. Alongside the main mechanic, there are mini-challenges such as shooting down small imps that curse the girls, adding an additional layer of strategy and timing. While the gameplay loop might seem repetitive on paper, the game balances it with varied enemy types, branching story paths, and multiple difficulty settings that keep things fresh and challenging for those seeking a deeper experience.

The narrative is delivered through vibrant, anime-inspired cutscenes and dialogue choices that determine which of several story routes the player will explore. The game features five main storylines, each focusing on different characters including the demon-hunting sisters Shinobu and Maya, who add a supernatural twist to the proceedings. The branching paths not only encourage replayability but also enrich the story world with different perspectives and character developments. Additionally, side quests and collectible items scattered throughout the levels provide incentives for exploration and completionists alike. Though the story leans heavily into ecchi tropes and fanservice, it is told with a lighthearted tone that often borders on self-aware comedy.

Visually, Gal*Gun: Double Peace delivers bright, colorful character models with expressive animations that bring the cast to life. The detailed designs of the girls and their exaggerated reactions underscore the game’s playful and irreverent tone. However, the environments themselves—mostly composed of generic school hallways and classrooms—lack the same level of detail, feeling somewhat sparse and repetitive as the player progresses through stages. The game performs well on most platforms, maintaining smooth animations and steady frame rates, though some ports, particularly on handheld devices, suffer from lower texture quality and occasional performance hiccups. The voice acting, fully in Japanese, complements the anime aesthetic with enthusiastic and emotive performances, further enhancing the immersive and often comedic storytelling.

Accompanying the visuals is a bubbly, upbeat soundtrack filled with catchy tunes that fit the game’s energetic mood. While the music is pleasant and memorable, the limited variety means it can become repetitive over longer play sessions. This is somewhat balanced by the frequent changes in dialogue and story sequences, which keep the player engaged on a narrative level. Sound effects—such as the clicking of shots and character reactions—are well executed, adding to the tactile feel of gameplay. Overall, the audio design supports the game’s lighthearted nature and maintains player engagement without becoming overwhelming or distracting.

Reception for Gal*Gun: Double Peace has been mixed but generally positive, with particular praise from fans of the genre and those who appreciate its quirky, unabashed style. On Steam, it holds a strong “Overwhelmingly Positive” rating, indicating that its niche audience finds significant enjoyment in its blend of gameplay and humor. Critics often commend the game for its addictive mechanics and replayability, especially praising the variety introduced by the multiple story paths and difficulty settings. However, some reviewers highlight its limitations, such as simplistic environments, occasional control issues (especially on PC), and a relatively short overall length. The game’s heavy reliance on ecchi elements also means it is not for everyone, which divides opinions among a broader audience.

Community feedback reflects these varied opinions, with many players embracing the game’s offbeat charm and replay value. Fans often point out the strategic depth hidden beneath the surface of what might initially seem like a gimmick-heavy shooter. The challenge of managing incoming enemies while trying to maximize score and affection meters keeps players invested, and the unlockable endings and badges provide motivation to revisit levels multiple times. On the other hand, some users express frustration with the control scheme on certain platforms, and a minority find the repetitive nature of the levels and music to be detracting from the overall experience.

In conclusion, GalGun: Double Peace stands as a distinct and memorable title that thrives on its wild premise and anime aesthetics. It may not cater to everyone’s tastes, especially given its overt fanservice and niche humor, but for those willing to embrace its absurdity, it offers a surprisingly deep, enjoyable, and replayable on-rails shooter experience. The combination of lighthearted storytelling, varied gameplay mechanics, and vivid character designs make it a noteworthy entry in the genre of Japanese visual novel shooters. Whether you are drawn by curiosity, comedy, or challenge, GalGun: Double Peace delivers an experience that is both entertaining and unapologetically unique.

No total tem 8 finais e entre eles dois finais secretos. Esses finais ajudam no fator replay do jogo que em diversas fases tem caminhos como direita ou esquerda, baixo ou cima que você pode seguir para conseguir bônus, coletáveis e completar as missões das garotas pela fase enquanto dispara seus feromônios carregados em outras garotas vestidas de colegial japonesa, vestidas com burama e roupas de banho que a proposito você pode trocar por outras skins especiais e skins de DLC. No tocante a gameplay, ela é básica de jogos de tiro em trilho, você avança e conforme as meninas que querem lhe ter/tomar/bater/beijar/tocar, você tem que disparar em uma das partes do corpo dela em que ela entra em euforia com mais facilidade, como por exemplo, a cabeça, o busto ou as pernas. O interessante é que cada garota tem seu ponto de euforia em uma parte diferente do corpo, podendo ser em um ponto especifico como a orelha direita. 
Conclusão: Jogo incrivel e a presidente do conselho estudantil tem muito resPEITO! E meu final favorito é o da Maya porém admito que o final da Shinobu talvez seja o final canônico. O final que vc fica com as duas não é muito legal.... OwO

II’ll be succinct. Yes, it’s a perverted game. And yes, it’s a very dumb fun though a little easy on-rails shooter of the likes like freaking House of the Dead or good old Umbrella Chronicles. Can only trust me on this.
A common run can be finished in around 2 to 3 hours. The player automatically moves through the map (there is cave even lol) and only has to focus on shooting. There are also side-missions per map on which you get extra cash that can use to buy upgrades like more damage or health. These upgrades remain as long as you use the same save. Once you start a new game, they also restart.

The story is extremely simple: Dude gets overcharged by a bad shoot from a Cupid; the love energy expelling from his body is going out of control and therefore makes the female student body from the setting to seek him out to take him as their partner, so they act as "enemies" that have to be shoot with "love" too to make them momentarily stop pursuing you. The story puts emphasis on four characters, two siblings with paranormal powers, the Cupid and a Demon that is making things difficult for the other three. There are multiple endings and you can even choose any of the normal adversaries to end up with the MC. 

As I said earlier, game is not a really a difficult shooter. There are some way over the line mini-games to ease the flow of shooting things. You do can enhance the difficulty by playing in harder difficulties or outright self-imposed challenges like not using upgrades. Music is cool, though there are little tracks.

If you don’t like anime, and or outright loathe the perverted/ecchi/sexualization in general of characters (because from a certain point of view, even the male MC gets it), don’t even try to cope your way into the series (Yes, I’m also adding the recent Metroidvanias here). These games were made as a celebration (devs’s words) of that specific genre of Japanese cartoons. The devs made the effort to craft a fun story with amusing gameplay full of the usual tropes and such, should be rated by what it offers instead of what it is. With that say if you are used to these shows or don’t mind and like on-rails shooter, give it a try; even better if you actually like old shows like To Love Ru, since the game doesn’t mind lampshading all the ridiculous clichés that come with the genre.

[b]●レールシューティングとしてのクオリティは意外と手堅い[/b]
[hr][/hr]
その軟派なゲームデザインとは裏腹に、レールシューティングとしてのクオリティは丁寧にしっかりと作られています。

女の子を一発で昇天させる性感帯…もとい弱点があり、それを繋げることでスコアやボムのゲージを上げたり。
ズームと共に透視できる機能がついているが、女の子の衣服を透けさせるだけでなく、オブジェクトを透視して隠されたアイテムを見つけたり。
周回プレイに耐えうるルート分岐や、買い物によるスキル強化など、お約束のシステムは概ね搭載されています。それでいて遊び心地はわりとイイ感じ。


[b]●モブの一人ひとりにさえも専用のエンディングがある[/b]
[hr][/hr]
ヒロインだけでもわりと多くのルートやエンディングが用意されています。

さらにこの類のゲームには珍しく、(テンプレに当てはめただけの簡素なものですが)モブの一人ひとりにも専用のルートやエンディングが用意されています。ヒロイン攻略中に推しができた際に、マニアックに一人だけを追い続けるプレイも可能。

全員に細かなプロフィールが設定されていて、それに沿ったセリフをシューティングパートでも投げかけてくれていたり、とにかくキャラ設定が細かく行き届いているのが嬉しいところ。


[b]●えっちなゲームとして「わかってる」演出[/b]
[hr][/hr]
基本的にはアホでえっちな雰囲気のゲームなので、とにかく都合の良いえっちハプニングが起こります。明るくて軽いノリが売り。
それでいてシューティングパートの視線移動がひたすらいやらしいのが「わかってる」感MAX。ベンチの下に潜り込んで見上げたり、天井裏やロッカーの中に隠れて覗いたり…

このあたりの演出はこのゲームの唯一無二な部分です。間違いなく。
今となってはちょっと古めなモデリングも、この演出が唯一無二であるからこそ良く見える部分もあります。


[b]●周回プレイはちょっと面倒[/b]

豊富なルート分岐やエンディングが用意されているにもかかわらず、ミニゲームやメッセージをスキップできないのが難点。
